beats.care: Bursting crackers on your street or footpath can break a court order. Use a permitted private space, prefer green crackers and respect time limits.
beats.what: On Oct 15, the Bombay High Court said its Sept 22 ban on bursting crackers on public roads now applies all year, for all festivals.
beats.why: The court is tracking noise and air pollution during festivals. It said the real problem is people not following the law.

opts: Bursting crackers on public roads and footpaths
cards.q: What exactly did the High Court stop?
cards.why: The bench said it has not banned manufacture, sale or festivals in general, only bursting in public places.

cards.body: The state, BMC and MPCB must set up an awareness plan within a week, with school sessions, announcements and boards in buses, stops and trains.
cards.caption: Deadline for an awareness drive

cards.body: Civic bodies, MPCB and police must set up ways to report violations, like special phone numbers or email IDs. A lawyer also suggested using the traffic police's complaint app.
cards.title: How will people complain?

cards.body: This started as a Ganesh festival order in September. The court has now stretched it to every festival, all year round.

cards.q: Would you report a neighbour bursting crackers on the road?

cover.label: Days a year: no crackers on public roads

hook: Can you still burst crackers *outside your building* this Diwali?

learn.t: The court did not ban making or selling crackers; it only stopped bursting them in public places like streets.

sources.name: Free Press Journal
sources.title: Bombay HC Extends Year-Round Ban On Bursting Firecrackers On Public Roads, Streets And Footpaths

tldr: The Bombay High Court says no one can burst firecrackers on Mumbai's roads, lanes or footpaths, on any festival, all year.
